S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and disturbances in how one experiences body weight or shape. It often begins in adolescence or young adulthood but can emerge or recur later in life, sometimes around major life transitions, illness, or losses. The course can be chronic or relapsing, with medical complications affecting multiple organ systems and significant psychosocial impairment, even when the person denies the severity. It is distinguished from other eating disorders by the combination of underweight status and the centrality of weight, shape, or weight-gain fears in the person’s self-evaluation and behavior.

patient.stressor: As Maria approached retirement from her long-term job as a building cleaner, she found the looming change unsettling, worrying about losing her routines, income, and sense of usefulness. Around the same time, her doctor mentioned that her blood pressure and cholesterol were "borderline," and she began trimming portions and skipping meals, telling herself she was just trying to "be healthier" for retirement and to avoid becoming a burden on her family. What began as modest dieting gradually turned into rigid food rules that clashed with her usual joy in cooking and sharing traditional Puerto Rican meals, leaving her increasingly isolated at family gatherings and church events where food is central to connection. Her husband and domino friends eventually urged her to see a doctor when they noticed her clothes hanging loosely and her reluctance to eat at social events, and after her primary care physician expressed concern about her low weight and asked about her preoccupation with staying "small" in this new phase of life, she was referred for psychiatric assessment.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately all I can think about is not getting bigger as I get older, and I judge myself by what the scale says more than anything else.”

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: Most days now I just pick at a little yogurt or a few crackers and tell my husband I already ate at work, and I’ve cut out rice, pasteles, and anything with oil because in my head those foods feel like they’ll go straight to my belly and make me huge for retirement.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: My uniforms hang off me and my wedding ring spins on my finger, but when my doctor or my sisters say I’m too thin, I shrug it off and think, ‘No, I still have a little pouch here, I should probably lose a bit more before I stop.’

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I even think about eating a full plate of food, especially things like pan sobao or pernil at a family party, I get this tight feeling in my chest and picture myself turning into one of those “chubby old ladies,” so I’d rather drink coffee or water and keep my stomach empty.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Every morning I weigh myself before work, and if the number is even half a pound higher I feel like a failure and spend the whole day replaying every bite I ate, like it proves I’m weak and not ready for this next stage of my life.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started turning down extra shifts and skipping our usual church potlucks and domino nights because I get so anxious about the food, and at home my husband and I argue more because he says he doesn’t recognize me and worries I’m disappearing right in front of him.
